requirements.statement: A success definition can declare, up front, an off-host proof for a must-pass criterion: a named CI job (workflow file and job name). The declaration is read deterministically from the definition; on a row that is not must-pass it is ignored and reported, never acted on.
requirements.source: Investigation O1 (PM instruction, 2026-11-12); Must pass: yes

requirements.statement: When a must-pass criterion with a declared off-host proof is triaged not-checkable-here, the loop checks that job's conclusion for the run's commit (gh run list / gh run view). A green job settles the criterion met, citing the CI run id and URL as evidence; a red, cancelled, still-running or absent job leaves it unproven, and the run ends must-pass-unproven as today.

The loop never accepts a gap by itself and never invents a proving environment at run time: a must-pass not-checkable criterion with no declared off-host proof still ends the run must-pass-unproven, and a must-pass criterion of kind build-defect or evidence-gap is never settled by an off-host proof, whatever CI says.
requirements.source: Investigation O3 (PM instruction, 2026-11-12, acceptance); Must pass: yes

requirements.statement: /refine-verification --auto may not add or change an off-host proof on a must-pass criterion (D16 of docs/TRD/verification-must-pass.md stands; the must-pass sentence of refine-verification.md's Owner rulings bullet and its --auto paragraph 'Access only the owner has is never guessed', pinned by refine-verification-must-pass tests).
Custody (packages/core/lib/custody.js) treats a CI-proven criterion like any other met criterion: it is re-proved when its covered files change and its proof is reused when they do not.
